name: Pluto
lede: A heart-shaped nitrogen plain and towering mountains of water ice — New Horizons made this dwarf planet unforgettable.

landmark.label: Sputnik Planitia
landmark.blurb: The bright western lobe of Pluto's heart — a vast nitrogen-ice plain with convective cells and no impact craters.

missions.name: New Horizons
missions.note: Historic flyby of Pluto–Charon; later visited Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth.

researchNotes: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt. Its atmosphere is thin nitrogen with methane and carbon monoxide; haze layers were imaged by New Horizons.
Sputnik Planitia is geologically young. Surrounding water-ice mountains can rise several kilometers. Charon is so large that the pair orbits a barycenter outside Pluto.
The IAU reclassified Pluto in 2006. It remains a premier laboratory for icy-world geology — reclassification did not erase New Horizons science.
folklore: Named for the Roman underworld god. Disney's dog and planet-status debates are pop culture; Sputnik Planitia is spacecraft geology.
carlFocus: Lead with Sputnik Planitia and New Horizons. Be clear it is a dwarf planet without dismissing the science. Mention Charon when asked about moons.
